concern_details.detail: main components involved in seat booking and their responsibilities
concern_details.why: The booking path is all there: Swing wizard and ReservationController, then LibraryFacade, ReservationManager, AssignmentStrategy, the domain model and the Registries. Each box has a one-line role that the code supports. Two weak spots. The StudyRoomManager role 'room and seat availability' does not say that it only feeds the wizard's availability screens before the booking (LibraryFacade.java:82-101, DateAndRoomSelection.java:214, AreaSelection.java:85). It plays no part in makeReservation. The domain model's role is a list of class names and does not say that it holds booking checks.

concern_details.detail: how they interact with each other
concern_details.why: The main call chain (UI to LibraryFacade to ReservationManager to strategy, domain, registries and notifier) is drawn and labelled. Some labels are wrong or vague. 'facade -> roommgr: queries availability' cites LibraryFacade.java:66, which is createStudyRoom. The real availability calls are at lines 82-101 and come from separate wizard steps, not from the booking call, and the diagram does not say this, so a reader may think booking goes through StudyRoomManager. 'validates, creates' on resmgr -> domain hides which checks are delegated: StudyRoom.isActive/isOpenOnDate, Area.getAvailableSeats, Seat.isAvailable and Student.hasActiveOrConfirmedReservationForDateAndSlot. The domain model in turn calls the registries (Seat.java:45, Area.java:51, Student.java:43), and only one of these calls is labelled. The view also never says that a rule violation surfaces as IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException, which RestExceptionHandler maps to HTTP 400.

concern_details.detail: which parts of the system may be affected by the modification
concern_details.why: The legend marks only ReservationManager and AssignmentStrategy as 'where booking rules live'. In the code, several existing rules sit in the domain model: weekday-only opening (StudyRoom.isOpenOnDate:141-147), seat availability (Seat.isAvailable:44-52), and one booking per student per slot (Student.java:42-50). ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot also decides which reservation states occupy a seat. A new rule may belong there too, so the domain model and ReservationRegistry are under-flagged. StudyRoomManager's availability screens must also reflect new rules, or the UI will offer seats that the booking then rejects. The legend does not say this. Persistence, DB and email are drawn with the same 'may be affected' styling, but a booking-rule change is very unlikely to touch them.

level_why: At the balanced level the developer needs the booking path and the places where rules live. The view goes two layers further. PersistenceManager and Reservations DB (MySQL) are generic infrastructure that no booking rule touches. NotificationServiceAdapter (email gateway) is likewise outside the change. These three boxes take up a quarter of the diagram while the rule locations inside the domain model stay hidden in one lumped box. Cutting them leaves about nine elements. The additions requested below are relabels or notes, not new boxes, so the view stays at the balanced level.
unsupported: facade -> roommgr 'queries availability' cites LibraryFacade.java:66, which is createStudyRoom. The relation exists through getAvailableStudyRooms, getAvailableTimeSlots and getRoomDetail (LibraryFacade.java:82-101), but those are separate wizard queries, not part of makeReservation. Drawn next to 'delegates booking' with no qualifier, it suggests that booking consults StudyRoomManager, and ReservationManager.makeReservation never calls StudyRoomManager.

The legend claims the blue elements are 'where booking rules live'. The code does not support that claim: the weekday opening, seat availability and per-student uniqueness checks are implemented in StudyRoom, Seat and Student (the domain model element), and the occupying-state logic in ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot. ReservationManager only orchestrates them and adds input and area/seat consistency checks.

The swing and rest elements are styled 'Faded = callers and external-facing edges' by the legend, yet the README presents them as parts that may need changes for new rule errors. The colour meaning and the README contradict each other.
missing: Which domain classes carry the existing booking checks, as a note or a member list on the domain model element: StudyRoom.isOpenOnDate/isActive, Area.getAvailableSeats, Seat.isAvailable, Student.hasActiveOrConfirmedReservationForDateAndSlot. The developer needs this to know where a new rule fits.

The domain model's lookups into the Registries for availability: Seat.isAvailable -> ReservationRegistry.findReservationsBySeat/occupiesSlot, and Area.getAvailableSeats -> StudyRoomRegistry. Only the Student lookup is labelled. A rule that changes 'what occupies a seat' lands in ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot.

How rule failures reach the user: IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException thrown by ReservationManager, mapped to HTTP 400 by RestExceptionHandler (boundary/SpringBoot/RestExceptionHandler.java:19-22) and shown by the Swing ReservationSummary. A short note on the rest/swing callers is enough; no new box is needed.
That StudyRoomManager's availability queries (the wizard's room, area and seat screens) must stay consistent with any new rule, which is why it counts as affected.
uml: Dependencies between components are drawn as solid arrows (-->), which reads as navigable association. A usage dependency in a UML component diagram is a dashed arrow, optionally «use» (..>).

Non-standard stereotypes <<accent>> and <<muted>> are used on components for styling. They are hidden in the render but remain in the model source. Highlighting should use a note or legend, not stereotypes.

AssignmentStrategy is a Java interface with implementation FirstAvailableAssignment, and it is the designed extension point for seat-choice rules. In UML it fits best as an interface that ReservationManager requires and the strategy component provides (lollipop/socket, or a realization). It is drawn as a plain component, so the extension point is not visible as such.

Reservations DB (MySQL) is drawn as a «component». If kept, it is an external database and would be better stereotyped (e.g. «database» is not standard; use a plain component/node with a note, or drop it per the level critique).
fixes: Show where booking rules actually live. Mark the domain model (and ReservationRegistry.occupiesSlot) as rule locations alongside ReservationManager and AssignmentStrategy, with a note listing StudyRoom.isOpenOnDate/isActive, Area.getAvailableSeats, Seat.isAvailable and Student.hasActiveOrConfirmedReservationForDateAndSlot. Fix the legend so it no longer claims that only the blue boxes hold rules.
Drop PersistenceManager, Reservations DB and NotificationServiceAdapter (or fold PersistenceManager into Registries) to reach the balanced level.

Relabel facade -> roommgr as the wizard's pre-booking availability queries (getAvailableStudyRooms/getRoomDetail, LibraryFacade.java:82-101), make clear that it is not part of makeReservation, note that it must stay consistent with new rules, and correct the evidence line.

Add a short note on the callers that rule violations surface as IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException, which RestExceptionHandler maps to HTTP 400 and the Swing ReservationSummary displays, so the affected UI and REST edges are explicit. Align the faded styling with this.

Use UML notation: dashed «use» dependencies instead of solid arrows, no custom stereotypes, and AssignmentStrategy shown as a required/provided interface (extension point) realized by FirstAvailableAssignment.
